exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, write the appropriate $$\varepsilon$$ - $$\delta$$ definition for each of the given statements.

solution.paragraph: For every $$ε>0,ε>0,$$ there exists a $$\delta >0,\delta >0,$$ so that if $$0<|t-b|<\delta ,0<|t-b|<\delta ,$$ then $$|g(t)-M|<ε|g(t)-M|<ε$$
For every $$ε>0,ε>0,$$ there exists a $$\delta >0,\delta >0,$$ so that if $$0<|x-a|<\delta ,0<|x-a|<\delta ,$$ then $$|\phi (x)-A|<ε|\phi (x)-A|<ε$$

problem.paragraph: An engineer is using a machine to cut a flat square of Aerogel of area 144 cm2. If there is a maximum error tolerance in the area of 8 cm2, how accurately must the engineer cut on the side, assuming all sides have the same length? How do these numbers relate to $$\delta,$$ ε, a, and L?

solution.paragraph: The engineer must cut within 0.328 cm of 12 cm on each side; $$ε=8,\delta =0.328,a=12,L=144ε=8,\delta =0.328,a=12,L=144$$

problem.paragraph: Use the precise definition of limit to prove that the following limit does not exist: $$\underset{x\rightarrow 1}{\lim }\frac{\left| {x - 1} \right|}{x - 1}.$$
Using precise definitions of limits, prove that $$\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\lim }f(x)$$ does not exist, given that $$f(x)$$ is the ceiling function. (Hint: Try any $$\delta < 1 \text{.)}$$

Using precise definitions of limits, prove that $$\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\lim }f(x)$$ does not exist: $$f(x) = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} {1 \text{if} x \text{is rational} } \\ {0 \text{if} x \text{is irrational} } \end{array} \right..$$ (Hint: Think about how you can always choose a rational number $$0 < r < d,$$ but $$\left| {f(r) - 0} \right| = 1 \text{.)}$$

Using precise definitions of limits, determine $$\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\lim }f(x)$$ for $$f(x) = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} {x \text{if} x \text{is rational} } \\ {0 \text{if} x \text{is irrational} } \end{array} \right..$$ (Hint: Break into two cases, x rational and x irrational.)
Using the function from the previous exercise, use the precise definition of limits to show that $$\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\lim }f(x)$$ does not exist for $$a \neq 0.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, suppose that $$\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\lim }f(x) = L$$ and $$\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\lim }g(x) = M$$ both exist. Use the precise definition of limits to prove the following limit laws:

solution.paragraph: $$lim x \to a f x + lim x \to a g x = L + M lim x \to a f x + lim x \to a g x = L + M$$

problem.paragraph: $$\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\lim }\left\lbrack {cf(x)} \right\rbrack = cL$$ for any real constant c (Hint: Consider two cases: $$c = 0$$ and $$c \neq 0 \text{.)}$$

$$\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\lim }\left\lbrack {f(x)g(x)} \right\rbrack = LM.$$ (Hint: $$\left| {f(x)g(x) - LM} \right| =$$ $$\left| {f(x)g(x) - f(x)M + f(x)M - LM} \right| \leq \left| {f(x)} \right|\left| {g(x) - M} \right| + |M|{\left| {f(x) - L} \right| \text{.)} }$$
